title: Meet Zendesk AI Agents: The most autonomous AI for customer service

hook.text: Meet the next generation of AI agents from Zendesk. Our AI agents don't just process tasks, they reason, they learn, they adapt...

summary.tone: Confident, calm enterprise launch: measured VO, soft green brand palette, clean recreated UI and plain-sentence title cards; one competitive jab ('All hype. No performance.') but otherwise polished and reassuring rather than energetic.

signature_moments.description: A 30 s split-screen chat demo where every agent turn on the left is mirrored by new chain-of-thought bullets (API triggers, agent hand-offs) on the right.
signature_moments.why_premium: It makes an invisible AI process legible: the viewer sees both the customer experience and the reasoning behind it, which is the product's core differentiator shown rather than claimed.

signature_moments.description: The opening chat widget plus chain-of-thought checklist returns as a bookend before the tagline, finishing with a slow push-in.
signature_moments.why_premium: Bookending gives the story a deliberate closed structure and reinforces one memorable product image, a hallmark of planned, storyboarded explainers.

signature_moments.description: The Z logo splits open and cycles service icons (chat bubble, thumbs-up, smiley, check) in its gap before closing and resolving into the lockup.
signature_moments.why_premium: A bespoke logo animation built from the brand's own geometry ties the mark to the product's purpose instead of a stock logo reveal.

hook.evidence: Opens instantly with the 'INTRODUCING AI Agents' title and a working chat-plus-reasoning UI while the VO makes a crisp contrast claim ('don't just process tasks, they reason, they learn, they adapt', w12-w21); strong, though a launch-style claim rather than a sharp pain or stat.

clarity.evidence: Clear arc: claim, one concrete banking use case, competitor contrast, two named features with chapter cards, accountability payoff and URL. The s003 and s010 screens are text-dense (181 and 147 on-screen words) and hard to read at speed.

ui_showcase.evidence: Simplified recreated UI tells the story well (chat thread mirrored by chain of thought in s003, procedure typed into the builder in s007, auto-built flow in s008), but s010 is a long static hold of a dense form with 0 events in anchors.

motion_polish.evidence: Clean, consistent motion (dot-to-pill chapter cards, staggered bubbles, dashed connector draw-on, logo split) but conservative and with long static holds: s003 runs 30 s, s010 runs about 18 s with 0 events, and several text cards simply hold.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchors plus visuals: a steady 120.19 BPM music bed under the VO, integrated loudness of -31.44 LUFS (quiet), and 111 SFX candidates that are mostly music or 'unsure' with swoosh_reverse CLAP labels, bunched in 0-16 s and 32-66 s; no clear accents line up with the chapter cards or the logo animation. Supportive but not distinctive.

vo_script_quality.evidence: Tight, benefit-led script with rhythmic triads ('they reason, they learn, they adapt', w16-w21), a relatable concrete scenario (missing reward for a family trip, w55-w81) and a clear payoff ('not just powerful, but can be held accountable', w245-w253); the competitor jab (w131-w154) is a little generic.

brand_consistency.evidence: One coherent system throughout: green/lime palette, repeated 'INTRODUCING' pill chapter cards, the same headline type on gradient cards, the opening UI returning as a bookend, and an end logo animation built from the Z mark.

works_muted.evidence: Key messages are on screen as text (s002 mechanism sentence, s005 'All hype. No performance.', feature chapter cards, s012 tagline, s013 URL) and the demos are self-explanatory; muted viewers lose the banking-scenario framing and the s004 competitor-race meaning.

overall.evidence: A well-structured, on-brand launch explainer that visualises AI reasoning convincingly and bookends neatly; held back from best-in-class by long static holds, dense text screens and a fairly anonymous sound bed.

localization_friendliness.notes: Heavy baked-in English: full-sentence title cards (s002, s005, s012), chapter cards (s006, s009), and text-dense recreated UI (s003 about 181 words, s010 about 147, s007 about 95) would all need re-rendering. The VO carries the banking scenario and the competitor contrast. The recreated (not screen-captured) UI helps, since strings could be swapped in the source project.

pattern.description: Cold open on a flat green gradient: a single dark dot pops in from zero scale just above centre, growing quickly and drifting up slightly before settling, synced to a soft pop.
pattern.why_premium: A single primitive on an empty brand-colour field gives a calm, confident first frame and a focal point that later shapes can build from, with the sound landing exactly on the appearance.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.fromTo('.dot', {scale: 0, y: 12}, {scale: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.45, ease: 'power3.out'}) starting on frame 1; trigger the pop SFX at the same time.
build_hint.remotion: const s = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 180}}); scale = s, translateY = interpolate(s, [0, 1], [12, 0]); no visible overshoot.

events.notes: The dot may be the first element of a Zendesk logo build (logo_resolve) in later events; cannot tell from this event alone, so 'other' is used. Energy decays smoothly with no rebound, so modelled as ease-out without overshoot.

pattern.description: After a hard cut from the title card to a flat green field, a dark-headed chat panel rises from below the frame and settles left of centre; then the customer's message bubble and avatar pop in and drift up into place.
pattern.why_premium: Two-step build: the container lands first with a long decelerating ease, and only after it is fully settled does the content arrive, so the eye reads the UI frame before the message. Flat background and generous negative space keep focus on one bubble.

build_hint.gsap: tl.fromTo(panel, {yPercent: 110}, {yPercent: 0, duration: 0.7, ease: 'power3.out'}); then tl.fromTo([bubble, avatar], {autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.9, y: 20}, {autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: 'back.out(1.4)', stagger: 0.05}, '+=0.3').
build_hint.remotion: panel translateY = interpolate(spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 100, mass: 1}}), [0,1], [height, 0]); bubble and avatar use spring({frame: frame - delay, config: {damping: 14, stiffness: 160}}) driving opacity, scale 0.9->1 and translateY 20->0.

events.notes: Energy spike at frame ~90 is the hard cut from the title card; the main motion is the panel rise. b02 is a diff region on empty green in the end frame (likely a transient position), so not used. SFX candidates sit on a regular percussive grid that looks like music; no clear designed SFX.

pattern.description: The AI agent's reply bubble and its avatar pop into the chat panel below the customer message and drift up a short distance while settling; the product card row begins to rise in beneath at the end.
pattern.why_premium: Reply arrives as one unit (avatar plus bubble) with a soft scale-and-rise that decelerates over about half a second, mimicking real chat arrival; the next content (product cards) is chained right after so the conversation keeps momentum.

build_hint.gsap: tl.fromTo([avatar, bubble], {autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.85, y: 40}, {autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: 'power3.out', stagger: 0.03}); tl.fromTo(cards, {autoAlpha: 0, y: 30}, {autoAlpha: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power2.out', stagger: 0.06}, '-=0.05').
build_hint.remotion: const s = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 120, mass: 1}}); bubble and avatar: opacity s, scale interpolate(s,[0,1],[0.85,1]), translateY interpolate(s,[0,1],[40,0]); cards use the same spring with delay ~30 frames and per-card stagger 2 frames.

events.notes: Filmstrip frames are a zoomed crop of the reply area. b01 is a union of bubble plus avatar and is not used to avoid double-counting. Product cards only start entering at the burst end (likely the next event). SFX candidates look like music beats.

pattern.description: A white 'AI agent chain of thought' card pops in top-right, connected to the chat by dashed lines, and grows as four checked steps append one after another, each with a green check icon.
pattern.why_premium: The card scales up in step with the list so the container never shows empty space; rapid ~100 ms stagger reads as the agent reasoning in real time and visualises an abstract claim ('they reason') as concrete steps.

build_hint.gsap: tl.fromTo(card, {autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.8, transformOrigin: 'left top'}, {autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.6, ease: 'power3.out'}); tl.fromTo(items, {autoAlpha: 0, y: 10}, {autoAlpha: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.2, ease: 'power2.out', stagger: 0.1}, '<0.05'); animate card height with the items (Flip or height: 'auto').
build_hint.remotion: card: spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 140}}) driving opacity and scale 0.8->1; items i: spring({frame: frame - 3*i, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 200}}) for opacity and translateY 10->0; card height interpolated from the visible item count.

events.notes: Dashed connector lines appear with the card (absent in the first frame of the crop) but have no candidate box; omitted rather than guessing a manual box spanning the card. Whether the card truly scales or only grows in height as rows append is ambiguous from the crops; filmstrip is a zoomed crop.

pattern.description: On a soft lime-to-white gradient, a three-line centred statement builds word by word in reading order, each word fading in at its final position; the full sentence holds once complete.
pattern.why_premium: Words land in place with no layout shift, so the reader tracks a stable centred block; the steady per-word cadence (roughly 2-3 frames apart) is fast enough to feel like a single reveal yet slow enough to read along. Large, tight sans type on a quiet gradient keeps it clean.

build_hint.gsap: Split the sentence into words (SplitText type: 'words'), then tl.fromTo(words, {autoAlpha: 0}, {autoAlpha: 1, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power1.out', stagger: 0.09}); lines are pre-laid out centred so nothing reflows.
build_hint.remotion: Map words with index i: opacity = interpolate(frame - i*3, [0, 7], [0, 1], {extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp', easing: Easing.out(Easing.quad)}); render inline-block spans in a centred fixed-layout block.

events.notes: Per-word diff boxes exist (b05-b17) but the 16 words exceed the 12-element cap, so lines (b02-b04) are used with text_unit word. Visible text runs ahead of the narration (line 1 is mostly shown before 'Powered' is spoken). Whether words also blur or rise slightly cannot be resolved from the filmstrip; no SFX candidates.

build_hint.gsap: tl.fromTo([bubble, avatar], {autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.92, y: 16, transformOrigin: 'right bottom'}, {autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: 'power3.out', stagger: 0.03}) at the narration word 'a' (~25.11s); text is static inside the bubble.
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame: frame - start, fps, config: {damping: 26, stiffness: 180, mass: 1}}); bubble and avatar style {opacity: interpolate(p,[0,0.4],[0,1],{extrapolateRight:'clamp'}), transform: `translateY(${(1-p)*16}px) scale(${0.92+0.08*p})`}; avatar delayed 1 frame; critically damped, no overshoot.
